# The Ultimately-Periodic Fingerprint

A Büchi automaton is **non-empty** iff it has a **reachable accepting cycle** — a *lasso*: a stem from the initial state to an accepting state $f$, then a cycle from $f$ back to $f$. Reading the stem once and the cycle forever gives an accepted word of the shape
$$ \alpha = u\cdot v^{\omega},\qquad u = \text{stem},\ v = \text{cycle}, $$
an **ultimately-periodic** word. Because a shortest stem and a shortest cycle each stay within the automaton, one can always find such a witness with
$$ |u| < |Q| \quad\text{and}\quad |v| \le |Q|. $$

This is the *fingerprint* behind emptiness (**[Notebook 14](14-buchi-emptiness-lasso.qmd)**): non-emptiness is not just a yes/no answer — it comes with a concrete, finitely-described infinite witness.

The automaton below is the editor that **saves infinitely often** (initial `open`, then it accepts iff `save` recurs forever). Pick a loop through the accepting checkpoint $f$ and read off the witness.

---

```{=html}
<script>
(function(){
  // BA
  const Q=['qb','q','f']; const init='qb'; const F=new Set(['f']);
  const delta={ qb:{open:'q'}, q:{edit:'q',idle:'q',save:'f'}, f:{edit:'q',idle:'q',save:'f'} };
  function edgesFrom(s){return Object.entries(delta[s]||{}).map(([sym,t])=>({sym,t}));}
  // shortest path src->dst (BFS), returns list of symbols or null
  function shortestPath(src,dst){
    const q=[{s:src,w:[]}];
    const visited=new Set([src]);
    while(q.length){
      const {s,w}=q.shift();
      for(const {sym,t} of edgesFrom(s)){
        const nw=w.concat(sym);
        if(t===dst && (nw.length>0)) return nw;
        if(!visited.has(t)){ visited.add(t); q.push({s:t,w:nw}); }
      }
    }
    return null;
  }
  const stem=shortestPath(init,'f'); // shortest u reaching f
  // loops: for each outgoing edge of f, sym + shortest path back to f
  const loops=[];
  for(const {sym,t} of edgesFrom('f')){
    if(t==='f'){ loops.push([sym]); }
    else { const back=shortestPath(t,'f'); if(back) loops.push([sym].concat(back)); }
  }
  // dedupe
  const seen=new Set(); const uniqLoops=loops.filter(l=>{const k=l.join(' ');if(seen.has(k))return false;seen.add(k);return true;});

  let chosen=0;
  function render(){
    const v=uniqLoops[chosen];
    document.getElementById('nb19-u').textContent=stem.join(' ');
    document.getElementById('nb19-u2').textContent=stem.join(' ');
    document.getElementById('nb19-v').textContent=v.join(' ');
    document.getElementById('nb19-v2').textContent=v.join(' ');
    // loop buttons
    const box=document.getElementById('nb19-loops'); box.innerHTML='';
    uniqLoops.forEach((l,i)=>{const b=document.createElement('button');b.className='loopbtn'+(i===chosen?' on':'');b.textContent='('+l.join(' ')+')ω';b.onclick=()=>{chosen=i;render();};box.appendChild(b);});
    // run
    const strip=document.getElementById('nb19-strip'); strip.innerHTML='';
    const seq=stem.concat(...Array(3).fill(v));
    let state=init; addStep(strip,'',state);
    const tail=new Set();
    seq.forEach((s,i)=>{state=delta[state][s]; addStep(strip,s,state); if(i>=stem.length) tail.add(state);});
    const hit=[...tail].filter(x=>F.has(x));
    document.getElementById('nb19-verdict').innerHTML=`<div class="verdict-box"><strong>Accepted.</strong> the loop returns to f&#8712;F, so f recurs infinitely often: In(&rho;)&cap;F = { f }. |u| = ${stem.length}, |v| = ${v.length}, both within |Q| = ${Q.length}.</div>`;
  }
  function addStep(c,sym,state){
    const box=document.createElement('div'); box.className='run-step';
    const s=document.createElement('div'); s.className='run-sym'; s.innerHTML=sym===''?'&nbsp;':sym;
    const st=document.createElement('div'); st.className='run-state'+(F.has(state)?' accept':''); st.textContent=state==='qb'?'q_b':state;
    box.appendChild(s); box.appendChild(st); c.appendChild(box);
  }
  render();
})();
</script>
```

The loop `(save)` gives the shortest witness `open·(save)ω = open save save save …`; the loop `(edit save)` gives `open·(edit save)ω`. Both are accepted, both are ultimately periodic, and both fit inside the state bound. Different lassos, same language — the witness is never unique, but one always exists whenever the language is non-empty.
